messages.subject: Support for IDate in scales
parts: It would wonderful to have support for formatting numeric data in IDate and ITime classes. The ITime class is just seconds in a day, so it should be very easy to implement.

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Support for IDate in scales
parts:
I've not looked at IDate or ITime, but if ITime is just seconds in the
day, it is similar to the times class in the chron package (where it is
a fraction, but the difference is a multiplicative constant). I wrote a
blog post awhile ago that tackled this problem.

http://blog.ggplot2.org/post/29433173749/defining-a-new-transformation-for-ggplot2-scales-part

Most of the work is in getting the transformation right. That is the
part that maps between your data type and part of the real number space
that can be used to position things on the plot. It also deals with
finding good breakpoints automatically and formatting labels. With a
working transformation, getting a full fledged scale is only a few lines.

There is an updated version of times_trans at

https://github.com/BrianDiggs/trans/blob/master/times_trans.R#L28

that dealt with issues right around 24:00. Getting the edge cases right
is always hard.

You could probably use some of this code as a starting point for writing
a transformation so that IDate and ITime could be used.
